rows.title: 11.1 A MODEL LIMIT NEVER ENDS A TURN (Noam 02.11 screenshot 17:5x: the turn stop

evidence.excerpt: | PLAN-1101 | 11. | 11.1 A MODEL LIMIT NEVER ENDS A TURN (Noam 02.11 screenshot 17:5x: the turn stop | Done | P3 | - |

evidence.detail: No owner acceptance or authenticated live behavior was exercised in this read-only task audit; code/declared completion is not current runtime proof.

evidence.body: A MODEL LIMIT NEVER ENDS A TURN (Noam 02.11 screenshot 17:5x: the turn stopped with 'Claude: request rate temporarily limited, the request was saved as blocked'; his words: 'needed to automatically transition to gpt models!'). ROOT CAUSE (read in the code, nothing called): the failover in src/desk_core/gateway.py runs Claude then Codex, but the moment ANY tool has started in the Claude attempt it stops the turn as 'blocked' (to avoid repeating an action), and it does not tell a harmless read (search, read a record) from an action that changes something; a rate limit that arrives after a read therefore ends the turn instead of moving to the backup, and the next message tries the limited provider again. SYSTEMIC FIX: (1) every tool the Desk can call is declared once as read-only or side-effecting in a registry (one owners-style file, a test fails for a tool with no declaration); (2) failover is blocked only after a SIDE-EFFECTING tool ran, and then the backup continues from a written 'what already ran' note instead of stopping; (3) a provider that answered rate_limit or login_needed is parked for its stated window (circuit breaker, a record), so the next turns go straight to the backup and nobody pays a failed first attempt; (4) the visible line names the switch in plain words ('answered by the backup model') and the health page shows the parked provider and when it returns; (5) the same breaker serves every Desk caller (chat, capture, judge, drafts). Check: a replay where Claude reads a record and then returns rate_limit yields an answer from Codex with the note; a replay where Claude sends a message and then hits the limit is reported with what ran and the backup continues without repeating it; ten turns after one rate limit make exactly one failed Claude attempt; done only on his words.

rows.title: 11.2 A BLOCKED REQUEST CAN BE RETRIED, AND A SHORT WORD NEVER GETS A GUESSED MEA

evidence.excerpt: | PLAN-1102 | 11. | 11.2 A BLOCKED REQUEST CAN BE RETRIED, AND A SHORT WORD NEVER GETS A GUESSED MEA | Done | P3 | - |

evidence.detail: No owner acceptance or authenticated live behavior was exercised in this read-only task audit; code/declared completion is not current runtime proof.

evidence.body: A BLOCKED REQUEST CAN BE RETRIED, AND A SHORT WORD NEVER GETS A GUESSED MEANING (Noam 02.11 screenshot 18:0x: the turn was blocked by the model limit, he wrote 'נסה עכשיו' (try now), and the Desk guessed he meant a new wording of an earlier intro message, wrote it, and added 'send the message' to today's list, none of which he asked; his words: 'another deep and massive failure that needs a structural fix e2e'). ROOT CAUSE: a blocked request is saved with 'no need to resend', but nothing connects a later 'try now / again / continue' to it, so the model is left to guess the antecedent from the last messages (same family as 8.14 and 8.17) and then acts on the guess (a task is filed, a draft is produced). SYSTEMIC FIX: (1) every blocked turn is a held thread with its original request id and text (7.1); (2) a retry door: a message that is only a retry word (a list of words, plus a tap on a 'try again' button that the blocked notice carries) is bound by CODE to the newest blocked request and replays that request's original text through the normal path, never through the model's guess; (3) a short or referring message with no certain antecedent gets ONE question card naming the two or three candidates, never an action; (4) nothing is added to the day list from a guessed meaning (8.15); (5) the blocked notice offers the button, so he never has to write the word. Check: replay of the 02.11 18:0x sequence (blocked turn, then 'נסה עכשיו') replays the blocked request exactly and files no task; a retry word with two blocked requests asks which; done only on his words.

evidence.body: THE CONVERSATION LIVES IN THE DATABASE AND EVERY TURN IS BUILT FROM IT (Noam 02.11 on the 'try now' failure: 'it should always have the conversation context! it should be in the db maybe?'). MEASURED TODAY: the live chat is a flat file (chat.jsonl); the database holds only his own words (8,149 rows in said) and 117 gateway rows, not the Desk's replies, blocked notices, cards or taps, and nothing links a message to the one it answers. So the context of a turn is whatever the file tail and the model's session happen to carry, which is why a short word after a blocked turn had no antecedent. This is plan 6.4 made a PREREQUISITE of 8.14, 8.17, 11.2: (1) table conversation_turns (id, who, text, kind: said/answer/blocked/card/tap, reply_to, request_id, state, topic/branch from 8.9, time), written by ONE door for every message in and out, never deleted; (2) the chat file becomes a generated reflection (like MASTER_PLAN.md), retired on the row-count proof of 4.2; (3) the context of EVERY turn, on every provider including the backup and a fresh session, is assembled by code: the last turns of the same branch verbatim with their reply_to links, plus every blocked or unanswered request, plus the map (8.9); the model never has to remember; (4) a taps and quoted replies arrive with the turn they answer (8.17). Build order: this item, then 11.2, 8.14, 8.17, 8.22. Check: kill the model session mid-conversation, send 'try now', and the next turn (on either provider) names the blocked request from the database; the row count of turns equals the lines of the old file; done only on his words.

I am giving it!'). THREE CAUSES, ONE INCIDENT: (A) the reply ended with the line 'Next I'm doing: ...': a terminal-only rule leaked into the window, because the Desk's agent is started with the same native user and project settings as a terminal session (gmail_hook_settings keeps them), so every terminal instruction (end-of-reply format, hooks, product-manager mode) also governs the window; (B) asked to research where and how to post Rough Cut on Reddit, it hit one blocked source (403 on the rules page), stopped, and told him the research 'was not completed', although other declared routes exist (the Reddit tool, search, cached rules); (C) the step needed his approval of the browser tool, and the Desk told him about it instead of raising the approval itself as one card with a button, then waiting. SYSTEMIC FIX: (1) the Desk's agent runs on its own settings layer: terminal-only rules are excluded by configuration (explicit setting sources and a Desk-only instruction file), and a test fails when a terminal-only rule phrase can appear; the reply judge also rejects internal protocol lines ('Next I am doing', ids, hook words) as defense in depth; (2) every research or fetch step has a declared route chain per source kind (primary, alternates, cache) stored once; a blocked route moves to the next, every attempt is recorded, and only a chain with no route left may be reported, with what was tried; (3) a step that needs his approval raises the approval itself (one card, one button, bound to the blocked step) and resumes by itself when he taps; (4) 'I will start now' is a held thread with an owner and a due time (7.1), never a sentence. Check: replay of the 02.11 18:1x exchange yields a rules answer from an alternate route or an approval card, no 'Next I'm doing' line, and no 'not completed' hand-back while a route is left; done only on his words.

evidence.body: OLD CONTEXT LOADS BY CONNECTION, BEFORE THE ANSWER (Noam 02.11: 'if I mention my surgery a month ago, will it know to load it before the surgery itself?'). HONEST STATE: today a turn loads (a) the newest turns, (b) records found by a keyword search on his words, (c) the branch cards of where his LATEST messages were placed; but the placement of the CURRENT message happens after the reply starts (the model places it during capture), so his current message does not pull its own branch, and the roughly 8,000 older turns have no place on the map at all, so an old surgery thread is reachable only by a lucky keyword. FIX: (1) a vocabulary per map node, learned from his own words that were placed there (table node_words), plus the node titles; (2) a fast placement of the incoming message by code, before the model starts (match against the vocabulary; ties and misses fall to the model placement and to one question); (3) the matched branch card is loaded WHOLE (every record, plan item, thread and his words homed there, any age, newest first, bounded to a fixed size with a pointer to the rest), so a mention of the surgery loads the surgery branch (health: surgery preparation) with its history; (4) a one-time backfill places the old turns on the map using a LOCAL model first and the Desk's own gateway slowly in the background, each placement a record with its source, no cloud test calls by an agent; (5) a miss is measured: a daily list of messages that matched no branch. Check: replay of 'the surgery' mentioned a month after its last message loads the surgery branch with the earlier turns before the first token; the share of old turns with a home is shown on the health page; done only on his words.

evidence.body: REVIEW ITEMS CLOSE FROM THE CONVERSATION, NOT FROM HIS MEMORY (Noam 03.11: 'I dont like keeping tasks in review that I dont remember to check because its so specific. can we set a reliable system that allows you to see the conversation and assess if things pass or fail by it?'). The conversation is already in the database (11.4, conversation_turns). FIX: (1) every item that waits for his words gets a probe in config/plan_checks.json: a trigger (what kind of message exercises it, by code: a priorities question, two requests in one message, a mention of an old topic, a subreddit read) and a pass/fail test over the Desk reply that followed (the same code checks the live review uses, e.g. helpfulness.check, answer_first.check, placement.foreign_subject; a local model only for what code cannot judge, never a cloud test call); (2) a daily step reads new conversation turns, finds triggered turns, runs the probes and records each verdict with the turn ids; (3) enough passes (a count per item, default 3, no fail) move the item to done with the turn ids as evidence; any fail moves it to in progress with the failing turn and reason; (4) the board shows per item: triggered N times, passed, failed, last turn; (5) he is never asked to remember to check; he is told only when an item fails or has had no trigger for a week (then it gets a one-line card 'try X'). Check: a seeded conversation with three passing priorities questions closes 8.14; one failing turn reopens it with the turn id; done only on his words about the system.

rows.title: Recommendation feedback and postponement memory

evidence.excerpt:
### TASK-1836: Recommendation feedback and postponement memory (🔄 IN PROGRESS)

**Priority**: P1 | **Status**: 🔄 IN PROGRESS (filed 2026-06-08) | **Depends on**: TASK-1833

**Why**: Research validation flagged that plans will keep feeling repetitive unless accept/postpone/dismiss actions become durable learning signals. Postponed work should not reappear every plan unchanged, and accepted work should become evidence of what the user actually follows through on.

**Scope**:

- Add a server-backed `recommendation_feedback` table or equivalent event type.
- Persist action, reason enum, optional free text, revisit date, recommendation/task IDs, and outcome signals.
- Downrank or hide postponed/dismissed suggestions until revisit/cooldown.
- Use accepted/time-blocked/completed/timer-started suggestions as positive follow-through signals.
- Link feedback to generated plan/recommendation IDs when available.
- Aggregate repeated explicit and implicit feedback into durable preference facts.
- Store `implicit_positive` signals from timer start/completion separately from explicit feedback.

**Acceptance**:

- A dismissed recommendation does not immediately reappear as a top suggestion.
- A postponed recommendation respects the revisit date.
- Feedback changes ranking evidence in later weekly/next-action responses.

**Progress**:

- 2026-06-08: Added mounted regression coverage that verifies a postponed weekly recommendation saves `generatedPlanId`, `recommendationId`, task/project entity key, reason category, revisit date, and becomes visually suppressed in the current plan.
- Feedback reason patterns become inspectable preference memory rather than hidden ranking magic.
- 2026-06-08: Broad non-weekly task-answer memory now retrieves recent `ai_recommendation_feedback` by UUID task IDs and text entity keys (`task:*`, `project:*`), so inline accept/postpone/dismiss signals can affect later broad answers even when task IDs are local or synthetic.
- 2026-06-08: Guest/localhost recommendation feedback now uses the same local AI-memory fallback as clarification answers. Local postpone/dismiss feedback is retrievable by task/entity key and derives parameter beliefs such as `energy_fit`, `ranking_focus`, and `task_recommendation_fit` for later suppression/reweighting.
- 2026-06-08: Broad fallback ranking now uses retrieved feedback directly: recent dismiss/postpone events suppress tasks until cooldown/revisit, simplify applies a smaller penalty, and accept/timeblock/implicit-positive events boost follow-through.
- 2026-06-08: Recommendation feedback now promotes conservative durable parameter beliefs after the raw feedback event is saved. Simplify/too-much updates `preference:brevity`, low-energy/too-hard updates `energy_fit`, not-important/wrong-context/needs-more-info updates `rankingFocus`, and accept/timeblock/implicit positives update `history`; rollout tests prove feedback still flushes even if the belief table is unavailable.
- 2026-06-08: Added direct broad fallback ranking regressions for local task IDs: dismissed cards are suppressed during cooldown, postponed cards stay hidden until revisit, inline project feedback does not suppress every task in the project, and accept/timeblock-style feedback boosts later follow-through ranking.
- 2026-06-08: Broad inline recommendation feedback now shows a visible saved/local status after postpone/dismiss-style actions, not only weekly-plan feedback. Localhost E2E proves postponing a broad inline card hides that exact card immediately and suppresses the same task from the next broad fallback answer without asking the same clarification again.
- 2026-06-08: Repeated recommendation feedback now aggregates into durable preference-level beliefs after three matching signals. Too-much feedback strengthens `preference:brevity`, low-energy/too-hard strengthens `preference:energy_fit`, weak-context/not-important feedback strengthens `preference:ranking_focus`, and repeated accept/timeblock signals strengthen `preference:follow_through`; broad and global memory retrieval now fetch those aggregate preference keys so saved learning can influence later chat answers instead of staying as isolated events.
- 2026-06-08: Weekly recommendation feedback now records the exact task entity key as the primary correction target and preserves project context as outcome metadata. Legacy project-key feedback from task cards is treated as task-specific when the recommendation ID names the task, so rejecting one weekly card does not suppress sibling tasks in the same project.
- 2026-06-08: Broad fallback ranking now has direct regression coverage for time-blocked and implicit-positive recommendation feedback, not only explicit accept. These follow-through signals boost matching tasks in later broad answers, protecting the required positive-learning path for accept/timeblock/timer-style outcomes.
- 2026-06-08: Added `ignore` as a first-class recommendation feedback action in TypeScript, migrations, schema contracts, local fallback memory, and broad fallback ranking. Ignored recommendations now create a mild ranking-focus backoff signal without fully suppressing the task, matching the research requirement for ignored suggestions to become learning data rather than disappearing as no-ops.
